confirmation_required.description: Whether the plan waits for `--yes`, or `yes` typed at the prompt.

items.description: Each item, in the order given.

total_allocated_bytes.description: The bytes on disk of the items to move or delete.

total_frees_bytes.description: What deleting them would free now, their sharers outside them kept.

expect_bytes.description:
`--expect-bytes`: what the plan must free, within 1%, before anything
is touched; null without it.

handle_count.description: How many items came from `--from` handles.

paths.description:
The items, absolute, as the plan names them: the paths, then the
handles' paths.

permanent.description: `--permanent`: delete the items rather than move them to the Trash.

yes.description: `--yes`: move the items, not only plan.

CleanResult.description:
The plan, and what acting on it did. Moving to the Trash frees nothing
until the Trash is emptied: `trashed_bytes` counts what moved, and
`freed_bytes` is set only by `--permanent`.

deleted_count.description: The items `--permanent` deleted, each with everything under it.

freed_bytes.description:
The bytes on disk `--permanent` freed, as `du` counts them: each
inode whose last link it removed, and each directory, including what
an item that failed part way had lost by then; 0 for the Trash, which
keeps what it holds.

plan.description: What would be moved or deleted, and what is refused.

trashed_bytes.description: Their bytes on disk, still taken until the Trash is emptied.

trashed_count.description: The items moved to the Trash.

hint.description: One imperative sentence naming a command; null when none helps.

retryable.description: Whether the same command may succeed if run again.

ExcludedEntry.description: A directory the scan listed but did not enter because of an exclude.

path.description: Its absolute path, as lossy UTF-8.

allocated_bytes.description: Bytes on disk: a directory's subtree, hard links and clones once.

error.description: Why moving or deleting it failed; null otherwise.

frees_bytes.description:
What deleting it would free now: its bytes less those a link or
clone member outside it keeps, measured from the tree for an item
that changed since the saved scan or whose bytes the scan does not
hold (a directory: what its walk found, at most), and with what a
walk found under a directory it holds but did not enter added; null
where that is not known (a directory a walk could not read whole, a
refused directory outside the scan's root, or one it did not enter).

links_outside_subtree.description: Links of the inodes under it that lie outside it.

name_raw.description: The name's bytes in base64 when they are not UTF-8.

nlink.description: A file's link count; null for a directory.

outcome.description:
`trashed`, `deleted` or `failed` once `clean` acted; null in a dry run
and for a refused item.

path.description: Its path, absolute, as lossy UTF-8.

path_raw.description:
The path's bytes in base64, only when they are not valid UTF-8 (its
own name's, or an ancestor's): the path to pass back.

reason.description: Why it is refused; null when it is not.

regenerable_by.description: The command that regenerates it, when a cache rule says so.

device_confined.description: Whether the scan stayed on the root's filesystem (`-x`).

error_count.description:
Directories that could not be read, and entries listed but not
read.

excluded.description:
The directories the excludes kept the scan out of within the path
read (at the scan's root, every one), path bytewise. A list verb's
envelope names the first 20 of them in the scan's order (pre-order,
siblings bytewise), and the warning `excluded_truncated` counts the
others; `summary` and `explain` name every one.

excluded_count.description:
Files left out and directories not entered by the excludes
(`--exclude`, `--exclude-from`, `--ignore-from`, `--exclude-caches`,
`--skip-containers`), in the whole scan. An incremental rescan counts
the files as the scan it renews counted them.

fallback_reason.description:
Why a rescan read the whole tree although it was not asked to:
`index_too_old`, `volume_changed`, `history_gone`,
`fsevents_disabled`, `options_changed`, `too_many_changes`,
`events_dropped` or `post_check_failed`; null for any other scan,
for a saved scan read back, whose index does not keep it, and on a
platform that keeps no change history (Linux), where every rescan
reads the whole tree.

fs_type.description:
The root volume's filesystem type; null when the scan recorded no
volume.

id.description: The saved scan's id; null for a scan that was not saved.

incremental.description:
Whether an incremental rescan wrote the scan: it read again only
what the volumes' change history (macOS's `FSEvents`) reports
changed since its parent, and took the rest from it.

parent_scan_id.description:
The saved scan this one scanned again (`rescan`); null for a scan of
its own.

rescanned_dirs.description:
The directories an incremental rescan read again; null for any
other scan, and for a saved scan read back, whose index does not
keep it.

root.description: The root, absolute, symbolic links resolved.

root_as_given.description: The root as the command line gave it.

size_kind.description:
The size the rows are ranked and shown by: `allocated` or
`apparent`.

total_allocated_bytes.description: Bytes on disk, hard links and clones counted once.

total_apparent_bytes.description: Apparent bytes, hard links counted once.

vanished_count.description: Entries that disappeared during the scan.

volumes.description:
The volumes the scan met within the path read, entered or not: the
one the path lies on, and those mounted at or under it; at the scan's
root, every one.

Tool.description: The program that wrote an envelope.

free_bytes.description: Bytes an unprivileged user can still write.

reason.description: Why not (`one_file_system`, `network`, …); null when it did.

code.description: One of the conventions' warning codes.

count.description: How many things it is about, where that applies.

hint.description: One imperative sentence naming a command.

description:
What `clean` prints under `--json`: the plan and what became of it, with
the conventions' error object where nothing, or not everything, was moved
or deleted (`ok` false): `confirmation_required`, `refused_path`,
`expectation_mismatch`, `trash_unavailable`, `path_changed`.

error.description: Why nothing, or not everything, was moved; null when all was.

next.description: Commands for the same scan, most useful first.

ok.description: Whether every item of the plan was moved to the Trash, or deleted.

result.description: The plan, and what moving it did.

scan.description:
The saved scan the plan's sizes come from; null when none holds the
paths and they come from a fresh `stat`.

schema_version.description: The version of the envelope's shape.

warnings.description: What the user should know beside the answer.

title: CleanEnvelope
